sources.entry: ngircd - Portable and lightweight Internet Relay Chat server for small or private networks. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 C/deb

summary.one_liner: ngIRCd is a free, portable, lightweight Internet Relay Chat (IRC) server written in C for small or private networks.
summary.what_it_does: ngIRCd runs as a single-node IRC server or as part of a network of ngIRCd servers across a LAN or the internet. It optionally supports IPv6, SSL/TLS for client-server and server-server links, PAM-based user authentication, IDENT requests, and character set conversion for legacy clients. The README says it implements most useful IRC commands and semantics used by existing clients, rather than every quirk of the original ircd. It includes user and channel modes and supports cloaking of users. Configuration is via a single config file, with documentation in a QuickStart guide and man pages ngircd(8) and ngircd.conf(5).
use_cases: host a private IRC chat server
run an in-house or small public IRC network
link multiple IRC servers into a network
IRC server with PAM login authentication
how_to_run: See INSTALL.md in the repository for build, install and upgrade instructions
Read doc/QuickStart.md for setup and running, including example configurations
Man pages: man 8 ngircd and man 5 ngircd.conf after installation
notable: Portable C source across many Unix-like platforms, Windows via WSL or Cygwin
Supports cloaking of users and many user/channel modes
Works fine with servers that have dynamic IP addresses
Included in package repositories of various operating systems
caveats: Designed for small or private networks rather than very large deployments
Windows support only via WSL or Cygwin
